evidence_status: Author-written synthesis; not an empirical design dataset, tested performance claim, trained model, or licensed asset library.

sources.influence: Subject-specific planning and critique; no copied design or universal aesthetic rules.
Atomic conditional guidance with contrasting weak and better examples; examples here are original social scenarios.
Locally retrievable structured guidance; no upstream palettes, font pairings, rankings or records copied.

patterns.use_when: A visible feature is the reason to care, and authorized imagery shows it.
patterns.avoid_when: The claim concerns an invisible outcome or the detail is absent from available material.
composition: Make the decisive detail large enough to recognize before reading the caption. Crop around its boundary, not through it.
Place one short observation beside the detail in a quiet area. Use an inset only when a wider view is needed for context.
In a sequence, move from whole subject to detail to consequence; avoid three identical product frames.
patterns.weak: A small shoe photograph below “Engineered for everything” leaves its claimed advantage invisible.
patterns.better: A real sole close-up identifies the actual tread geometry; the caption describes the visible feature without promising untested grip.
adapt: For an audience unfamiliar with the object, include a whole-object view; experts may need measurement or material context.
For an expressive brand, allow a bold crop; for an archival brand, show an orderly detail plate. Preserve approved typography in both.
patterns.check: Can the viewer point to the detail supporting the headline? Is any claimed benefit stronger than the supplied evidence?

patterns.use_when: The audience must choose between real alternatives and the same comparison basis is available.
patterns.avoid_when: Differences are unverified, unlike things are presented as equivalent, or one option is deliberately photographed worse.
composition: Keep viewpoint, scale, labels and units consistent across alternatives.
Give the decisive difference visual emphasis; keep shared details subordinate.
If two columns become cramped on a phone, give each option its own slide and end with a concise decision rule.
patterns.weak: Two unrelated room photos labeled “before” and “after” imply a result they do not establish.
patterns.better: Two authorized images of the same bag show what fits in each size, with confirmed dimensions and identical object scale.
adapt: A novice may need a familiar reference object; a specialist may need exact specifications.
An energetic identity can use an edge-to-edge split; a quiet identity can use aligned plates. Neither treatment changes the comparison evidence.
patterns.check: Are scale and conditions fair, and can the audience tell which option suits their situation without assuming a universal winner?

patterns.use_when: A real sequence or clearly labeled demonstration shows how one state becomes another.
patterns.avoid_when: Only final imagery is available, or a missing intermediate step would force an invented process.
composition: Establish the starting state, keep a stable visual anchor, then isolate the action that changes it.
Use arrows or numbering only for actual causal or temporal order.
Hold the changed detail long enough to inspect; place qualifications at the relevant step rather than hiding them in the ending.
patterns.weak: A software post replaces a messy screenshot with a pristine dashboard and claims the product removed all manual work.
patterns.better: A consented screen recording follows one request through assignment, showing the automation and the remaining human review.
adapt: New users need the initial problem named; experienced users need the exceptional step or constraint.
A craft brand can retain hands and material sounds; a software brand can retain the actual cursor and interface. Do not manufacture either.
patterns.check: Does the sequence show the mechanism, including remaining work, rather than just asserting a transformation?

patterns.use_when: A truthful sensory or emotional experience is itself the intended payoff.
patterns.avoid_when: The brief needs detailed instructions, evidence of efficacy, or multiple competing offers.
composition: Let one meaningful scene occupy the dominant area; position type using the actual light, movement and negative space.
Keep necessary product or event identification legible but secondary to the experience.
For video, use a subject-driven reveal or held moment; introduce cuts when attention or information changes, not at arbitrary fixed intervals.
patterns.weak: A generic sunset and “Experience the extraordinary” could advertise any destination or product.
patterns.better: An authorized close view of steam escaping the bakery’s actual morning loaf communicates warmth; confirmed availability belongs in the caption.
adapt: Choose a sensory detail this audience values: texture, sound, scale, companionship or anticipation.
Translate mood through the brand’s existing photo treatment and pace; do not assign muted colors or slow motion to every premium brand.
patterns.check: Is the scene specific to this offer, and is atmosphere being mistaken for proof of origin, quality or outcomes?

patterns.use_when: An authorized document, sample, quotation or measured observation can substantiate a narrow point.
patterns.avoid_when: Permission, source, scope or relevant context is missing; a mockup would resemble authentic evidence.
composition: Show the evidence-bearing portion at readable scale, with necessary context nearby.
Separate observation from interpretation using hierarchy or distinct regions, not decorative data widgets.
A carousel can show the artifact, explain the relevant detail, then state the limits or practical implication.
patterns.weak: A giant “98%” with a decorative chart implies performance without a source or denominator.
patterns.better: A permitted test sample identifies the observed measurement, conditions and source; the headline states only what that sample supports.
adapt: Experts may need method and units on the artwork; general audiences may need a plain-language interpretation and accessible source in the caption.
Use the brand’s document or editorial vocabulary without adding fake seals, awards or institutional authority.
patterns.check: Can a reviewer trace the claim to this exact artifact, and are scope, permission and uncertainty visible where needed?

patterns.use_when: A real event or offer has both an experiential reason to attend and verified practical details.
patterns.avoid_when: Date, venue, price or availability is uncertain and cannot be clearly marked as provisional.
composition: Use an actual scene, performer or object to convey what is distinctive about the occasion.
Group what/when/where in a coherent readable block; give the next action a real destination.
For a carousel, establish the experience first, then practical details; ensure the first slide identifies the occasion when shared alone.
patterns.weak: A poster buries the date in ornate texture while “You don’t want to miss this” dominates.
patterns.better: A permitted rehearsal photograph carries the concert’s character; a clean adjacent block states the confirmed date, venue and booking route.
adapt: A returning community may recognize the subject; newcomers need a plain description and access context.
An exuberant identity may use lively lettering around a clear logistics block; a restrained identity may let the scene carry expression.
patterns.check: Can someone identify the occasion, time, place and next action at viewing size without interpreting decorative symbols?

patterns.use_when: A small set of supported conditions changes what the audience should do.
patterns.avoid_when: Advice is high stakes without qualified support, or the conditions are speculative.
composition: Lead with the audience’s actual situation; show the discriminating question before the options.
Use parallel branches only when choices really branch. Put one useful example at the point of ambiguity.
For a single image, reduce to one decision; use a carousel when explanation cannot remain readable.
patterns.weak: Five generic tips repeat “choose what works for you” and end with an unrelated sales CTA.
patterns.better: A verified garment size guide shows which measurement to take, how it maps to this maker’s chart, and what to do between sizes.
adapt: A novice benefits from a demonstration; an experienced audience needs the unusual exception.
Use the owner’s instruction tone and illustration system. A playful voice can stay precise, and a formal voice can stay approachable.
patterns.check: Could someone actually make the intended choice, and does every branch follow from available evidence?

patterns.use_when: A specific person, object or occasion has a truthful narrative or an explicitly fictional joke.
patterns.avoid_when: The story requires invented testimonials, cultural stereotypes or false behind-the-scenes claims.
composition: Open on the particular tension or surprising detail, not a generic manifesto.
Vary visual distance as the story develops: context, action, revealing detail, payoff. Reuse a visual anchor so variation remains coherent.
Let the ending resolve the opening. Add an action only if it follows naturally from the payoff.
patterns.weak: A maker’s story uses anonymous stock hands and “Passion meets perfection” without saying anything particular.
patterns.better: Authorized workshop photographs follow one real glaze trial, including an imperfect sample and the maker’s approved explanation of what changed.
adapt: Match how much context the audience already has; an inside joke needs a community that understands it.
A dry brand may use a concise visual punchline; a warm brand may linger on human detail. Keep the story specific in either voice.
patterns.check: Does the ending deliver something the opening promised, and can every factual scene or quotation be traced to permission and source?
